claims.text: The starting material is additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
The as-built alloy has a primarily FCC matrix.
The as-built alloy contains intrinsic microstructural heterogeneities produced by additive manufacturing.
Post-process annealing promotes grain-boundary segregation and precipitate formation.
Annealing-enhanced diffusion causes alloying elements to segregate at grain boundaries.
Segregated grain-boundary regions are preferential sites for accelerated oxidation or reduction.
Elevated-temperature oxidizing or reducing exposure forms brittle reaction products along grain boundaries.
Brittle intergranular reaction products compromise grain-boundary cohesion.
Loss of grain-boundary cohesion initiates and propagates microcracks that can culminate in catastrophic failure.
Relative to as-built specimens, annealed specimens will exhibit more pronounced grain-boundary precipitation.
Relative to as-built specimens, annealed specimens will exhibit more extensive intergranular oxidation or reduction products after identical exposure.
Relative to as-built specimens, annealed specimens will exhibit more intergranular cracking.
Relative to as-built specimens, annealed specimens will have lower fracture toughness after exposure.
The as-built baseline has more uniform grain-boundary chemistry than the annealed state.
The as-built baseline is less susceptible to accelerated intergranular degradation than the annealed state under identical exposure conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies at temperatures of at least 700 degrees Celsius during prolonged exposure to sufficiently aggressive oxidizing or reducing atmospheres.
